rejected.title: Casual and gig work
card: Casual work
a job with no promise of ongoing work. Hours can change from week to week, and casual employees get no paid sick leave or holiday pay.
Casual loading
a higher hourly rate that most casual employees get instead of paid leave. It is often 25% more than the rate for a permanent worker.
Gig work
short jobs or tasks, often found through an app, such as delivering food. Gig workers are paid for each job and often get no paid leave.
More Australians now work casual or gig jobs. Many like the flexibility of choosing when to work, but their income can be uncertain.
rejected.remember: Casual and gig work give flexibility, but often less certain income and no paid leave.

a.q: Sam delivers meals through an app and is paid for each delivery. Which describes his work?
opts: He can often choose which hours he works
He gets paid holiday leave each year
He is promised the same hours every week
He gets paid sick leave when he is unwell
a.why: Gig work found through an app often lets workers choose when to work, which is its flexibility. Gig workers often get no paid leave and have no promise of certain hours.
a.clue: Think about how gig jobs are found and paid.

b.q: Jess is a casual employee at a Darwin café. She is sick one week and misses her shifts. What is likely to happen?
opts: She is not paid for the shifts she misses
She gets paid sick leave for the shifts she misses
She gets casual loading for the shifts she misses
She is promised the same shifts next week
b.why: Casual employees get no paid sick leave, so Jess is not paid for the shifts she misses. Casual loading is a higher rate on the hours she works, not pay for shifts she misses.

draft.title: Casual and gig work
card: Casual work
a job with no promise of ongoing work. Casual workers often have no paid sick leave or holiday pay, and their hours can change from week to week.
Gig work
short jobs or tasks, often found through an app, such as delivering food or driving passengers. Gig workers are paid for each job.
More Australians now work in casual or gig jobs. Many people like the flexibility, such as choosing when to work.
The cost of this flexibility is that income can be uncertain. Workers may have no sick leave, no holiday pay and no certain hours.
draft.remember: Casual and gig work give flexibility, but often with less certain pay and no leave.

a.q: Which is the main benefit of gig work for a worker?
opts: Flexibility to choose when to work
Paid holiday leave each year
Certain hours every week
Paid sick leave when unwell
a.why: Gig workers can often choose when they work, which is the flexibility the card describes. Paid leave and certain hours are what these jobs often lack.
a.clue: Think about what workers gain, not what they miss out on.

b.q: Jess works casual shifts at a Darwin café. She is sick one week and cannot work. What is likely to happen?
opts: She may not be paid for the shifts she misses
She is paid sick leave for the missed shifts
She is paid extra for being flexible
She has certain hours for the next week
b.why: Casual workers often have no paid sick leave, so missed shifts may mean no pay. Being flexible does not bring extra pay, and casual hours can change from week to week.
b.clue: Casual work often has no sick leave.

a.best: Flexibility to choose when to work

b.best: She may not be paid for the shifts she misses
